overview: A self-managing, icon-only camera/video control button for Zoom Video SDK sessions. On tap it starts or stops the local participant's video based on current state. It registers as a delegate observer and automatically keeps its icon synchronized with the authoritative SDK video status. Unlike ZMUIToolkitAudioBtn, there is no separate 'join' state; video is simply on (unmute) or off (mute).

typeDefinitions.name: VideoButtonType
typeDefinitions.note: Case names describe the CURRENT state, not the tap action. In .unmute (video on) a tap stops video; in .mute (video off) a tap starts video.

typeDefinitions.name: ZMUIToolkitIconBtn
typeDefinitions.notes: UIButton subclass providing icon/badge/layout configuration and click callback dispatch.

typeDefinitions.name: ZMUIToolKitManager
typeDefinitions.role: holds ZoomVideoSDK instance and videoSDKDelegate fan-out

typeDefinitions.name: CompositeZoomVideoSDKDelegate
typeDefinitions.role: weak fan-out delegate; register via add(_:) / remove(_:)

typeDefinitions.name: ZoomVideoSDKVideoStatus
typeDefinitions.notes: Returned by videoStatus(); the 'on' boolean indicates whether video is live.

prerequisites: Zoom Video SDK initialized and registered with the toolkit via ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize(videoSDK:bundleId:) BEFORE constructing the button.
Construct and use on the main thread (@MainActor).
lifecycle.ifNotInitialized: If ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDK is nil, videoStatus()?.on resolves to false so the button constructs in the 'mute' state, and tap actions take no effect (the callback proceeds only when the video helper, video status, and self are non-nil).

actions: build descriptor (40x40, clear bg, secondaryLabel icon color, zero padding)

exitPoints.note: Delegates are held weakly; removal is defensive.

lifecycle.delegateModel: The button does NOT assign itself to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate. It registers with the toolkit fan-out delegate ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate (CompositeZoomVideoSDKDelegate), enabling multiple observers. Child delegates are stored weakly.

stateTransitions.condition: authoritative; only when local user is in changed list

threadingNotes: The current state is decided in the tap callback by reading videoStatus()?.on. Both stopVideo() and startVideo() are invoked directly from the button's @MainActor tap path, and the optimistic switchTo(...) updates run on the main thread. The displayed state is reconciled by onUserVideoStatusChanged.

apis.name: init
apis.description: Reads local video status (getMySelf()?.getVideoCanvas()?.videoStatus()?.on) to choose initial state/icon, constructs the button, registers as a delegate observer, and syncs state.

apis.name: init(coder:)
apis.description: NOT SUPPORTED. Calls fatalError. Do not instantiate from Storyboard/XIB.

apis.name: setMuteVideoIcon
apis.description: Overrides the icon used for the 'mute' (video off) state. Applied immediately if currently in the mute state.
sideEffects: Updates muteIcon; calls switchTo(.mute) if currentType == .mute

apis.name: setUnmuteVideoIcon
apis.description: Overrides the icon used for the 'unmute' (video on / live camera) state. Applied immediately if currently in the unmute state.
sideEffects: Updates unmuteIcon; calls switchTo(.unmute) if currentType == .unmute

apis.name: switchTo
apis.description: Sets currentType and updates the displayed image to match. Internal; documented for completeness.
sideEffects: Sets currentType and the normal-state image

apis.name: syncCurrentState
apis.description: Recomputes state from the SDK's current video status and calls switchTo(type:). Called from init, didMoveToWindow, onSessionJoin, onUserVideoStatusChanged.

apis.name: didMoveToWindow
apis.description: UIView override. Refreshes the icon to the current SDK video state when the button is attached to the view hierarchy.

inheritedConfiguration.warning: Do not use setIcon/setImage to represent video state; it is transient and overwritten on the next resync. Use the per-state set*VideoIcon methods.

callbacks.name: onSessionJoin
callbacks.description: Fired when the local user joins the session. Resyncs the icon to the SDK video status.
callbacks.stateChange: resyncs to match SDK video status

callbacks.name: onUserVideoStatusChanged
callbacks.signature: public func onUserVideoStatusChanged(_ helper: ZoomVideoSDKVideoHelper?, user users: [ZoomVideoSDKUser]?)
callbacks.description: Fired when any user's video status changes. Filters to the local user by ID and resyncs only when the local user is in the changed list. Primary mechanism for authoritative icon state (e.g. video started/stopped externally, by the host, or by the system).
callbacks.stateChange: resyncs to match SDK video status for local-user changes only
inactiveConditions: local user ID cannot be resolved
local user not in changed list

outcomeHandling.strategy: The tap callback inspects the ZoomVideoSDKError returned by each video-helper call. The icon updates ONLY on .Errors_Success; otherwise the icon is unchanged and the onUserVideoStatusChanged callback reconciles state.

perAction.onOther: icon unchanged; reconciled by delegate resync

perAction.execution: direct call on the main actor
perAction.onOther: icon unchanged; reconciled by delegate resync

outcomeHandling.reconciliation: The displayed state is reconciled by onUserVideoStatusChanged. To respond to outcomes, observe SDK events via your own ZoomVideoSDKDelegate registered with ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.add(_:).

required: Initialize the toolkit (ZMUIToolKitManager.initialize) before constructing the button.
Construct and use the button on the main thread.
forbidden: Instantiating via init?(coder:) / Interface Builder (traps with fatalError).
Assigning the button (or anything) directly to ZoomVideoSDK.delegate; use ZMUIToolKitManager.videoSDKDelegate.add(_:).
Using inherited setIcon/setImage to represent video state; it is overwritten on next resync.
